name: California
structure: own CalEITC schedule (calculated independently of the federal credit): max credit $313 (no children) / $2,088 (1) / $3,447 (2) / $3,878 (3+); earned income cap $34,050 for every family size and filing status
notes: No percentage of the federal credit is used: the FTB table published with the 2026 instructions shows the CalEITC maximum credit is about 47% of the corresponding federal maximum (TPC, same table). The FTB page fetched on 2026-10-26 still shows the tax year 2025 table (income cap $32,900; max credit $302/$2,016/$3,339/$3,756); the 2026 figures ($34,050; $313/$2,088/$3,447/$3,878) were read from a secondary reproduction of the FTB 2026 table. maxIncomeSingle and maxIncomeMarried are the same because the FTB income cap does not vary by filing status.

name: Colorado
notes: COLORADO DOR states 25% of the federal credit for 2026 and later, down from 50% in tax year 2025 (TPC and NCSL both list 50% because they publish the tax year 2025 table). Colorado DOR also states that after tax year 2026 the percentage moves between 25% and 50% depending on state revenue conditions. CRS 39-22-123.5 as quoted in the Colorado fiscal note shows a base 20% for 2026 and later, so the 25% rate comes from the revenue-trigger provision; TPC/NCSL/IRS are stale here.

name: Connecticut
structure: 40% of the federal EITC plus a flat $250 for filers who have at least one federal qualifying child
asOf: tax year 2025 and later (CT DRS page, current)
notes: The $250 addition is stated by CT DRS on the same page and is not reflected in TPC/NCSL/IRS. Structure is not a plain percentage because of the flat addition.

name: Delaware
structure: taxpayer choice: 4.5% of the federal credit as a refundable credit, or a 20% nonrefundable credit
notes: TPC footnote: Delaware also offers a nonrefundable 20% credit. NCSL lists the same 4.5% refundable / 20% nonrefundable pair. No separate Delaware income limit is published in these sources; eligibility follows federal EITC eligibility.

name: District of Columbia
notes: DC OTR table: 100% for tax year 2025, 85% for 2026-2028, 100% from 2029. TPC (2026-07-14) and NCSL still show 100%, which is the tax year 2025 rate; IRS (26-Nov-2025) shows 70%, the tax year 2024 rate.

name: Hawaii
notes: No change for 2026 found in the ITEP 2027 brief (15-Sep-2026) or in the IRS/NCSL tables. No separate Hawaii income limit is published; eligibility follows federal EITC eligibility.

name: Illinois
notes: Also matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found. No separate Illinois income limit is published.

name: Indiana
notes: The Indiana EITC is available only to taxpayers with at least one qualifying child. Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Iowa
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Kansas
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Louisiana
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Maine
structure: 25% of the federal credit for all other eligible filers; 50% for filers without dependent children
asOf: tax years beginning on or after 2022 (Maine Revenue)
notes: Maine Revenue states 25% (50% without qualifying children) for tax years beginning on or after 2022. TPC and NCSL publish the same pair. The 50% variant means this is not a plain single percentage.

name: Maryland
structure: 45% refundable for filers with qualifying children or married couples; 100% refundable for filers without qualifying children; a nonrefundable 50% credit is offered as an alternative (not both)
asOf: tax year 2025 instructions (45% rate made permanent)
notes: TPC footnote gives the same three rates (45% / 100% / 50% alternative). NCSL shows '100% or 50%' and does not mention the 45% refundable rate for filers with children, so TPC plus the Maryland booklet is the better source. Maryland localities also offer their own EITC. No separate Maryland income limit is published; eligibility follows federal EITC eligibility.

name: Massachusetts
notes: NCSL shows 30% and is out of date; TPC (2026-07-14) and the IRS table (26-Nov-2025) both show 40%. Massachusetts raised the credit to 40% for tax year 2025. No change for 2026 found.

name: Michigan
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Minnesota
structure: 4% of earned income up to a maximum credit of $379; the credit phases out above $31,950 (single, head of household, married filing separately) and $37,910 (married filing jointly)
notes: Not a percentage of the federal credit, so percent is null. TPC lists the Minnesota maximum credit as $369 for tax year 2025 while the Minnesota DOR page and its 2026 publication show $379 with the phase-out thresholds $31,950 / $37,910; the DOR figures are used. No separate Minnesota income cap exists beyond these phase-out thresholds. The 2026 tax year values were not published in the sources checked.

name: Missouri
asOf: tax year 2024 and later (Missouri DOR FAQ)
notes: Missouri DOR: the credit is 20% of the federal EITC for tax year 2024 and later, and it is not refundable (it offsets tax owed). NCSL lists '10% to 20%' because the statute sets 10% and allows an increase; TPC lists 20%.

name: Montana
notes: Montana HB 337 raised the credit from 10% to 20% of the federal credit beginning in tax year 2026; TPC's footnote confirms 'For 2026, Montana expanded its state EITC to be 20 percent'. The TPC table itself still shows 10% because it is the tax year 2025 table, and NCSL shows 20% already.

name: Nebraska
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: New Jersey
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: New Mexico
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: New York
notes: TPC footnote: New York City adds a local EITC of 10% to 30% of the federal credit, depending on income and number of qualifying children. That city layer is not in this table.

name: Ohio
notes: Nonrefundable: it can only offset tax owed. Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Oklahoma
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: Oregon
structure: 14% of the federal credit for all other eligible filers; 17% when the youngest qualifying child is under age 3
notes: Oregon Form OR-40 instructions, revision 09-11-26 (for tax year 2026, filed in 2027), Table 6: 14% (0.14) for a youngest dependent aged 3 or older or no dependents, 17% (0.17) for a youngest dependent younger than 3. TPC's footnote confirms the 2026 expansion from 12% / 9%. NCSL still shows 9% / 12% and is out of date.

name: Pennsylvania
asOf: tax year 2025 and tax year 2026 (Pennsylvania DOR)
notes: Pennsylvania DOR: the state credit equals 10 percent of the federal credit and applies beginning with the 2026 tax season, so the first claims were on tax year 2025 returns (maximum $805 for tax year 2025). TPC and NCSL list 10% as well. No separate Pennsylvania income limit is published.

name: Rhode Island
notes: Matches NCSL and IRS. No change for 2026 found.

name: South Carolina
structure: 125% of the federal credit, capped at $200 starting in tax year 2026, for full-year South Carolina residents
notes: South Carolina DOR: H.4216 caps the credit at $200 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 and limits it to full-year residents. TPC and NCSL list 125% without the cap. The credit is nonrefundable.

name: Utah
structure: lesser of 20% of the federal credit or 20% of Utah wages reported on the W-2 form
notes: Utah Code 59-10-1044 limits the credit to the lesser of 20% of the federal EITC or 20% of the taxpayer's Utah wages; it is not refundable. TPC and NCSL both list 20% and nonrefundable.

name: Vermont
structure: 38% of the federal credit for filers with qualifying children; 100% for filers without qualifying children; prorated for part-year residents
notes: 32 V.S.A. 5828b: 38% of the federal credit for filers with qualifying children and 100% for filers without qualifying children, prorated for part-year residents. TPC and NCSL list only the 38% figure.

name: Virginia
structure: 20% refundable for tax years 2025 and 2026; a 20% nonrefundable credit remains available as an alternative; full refundability becomes permanent from 2027
notes: Va. Code 58.1-339.8: for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 but before January 1, 2027 the refundable credit is 20% of the federal credit, with the 20% nonrefundable credit as an alternative; from 2027 the credit is fully refundable. NCSL lists 15% refundable / 20% nonrefundable, which is the pre-2025 rate.

name: Washington
structure: Working Families Tax Credit with a flat-dollar schedule: $335 (no children) / $660 (1) / $995 (2) / $1,330 (3+), reduced on a scale that depends on the number of qualifying children; eligibility income thresholds are the federal EITC thresholds
notes: Washington calculates the credit independently, so percent is null. TPC footnote: the WFTC refund scales use reduction percentages that depend on the number of qualifying children. NCSL publishes the same dollar amounts. The 2026 tax year amounts were not published in the sources checked. From 2029 the credit expands and the age floor drops to 16.

name: Wisconsin
structure: 4% of the federal credit for one qualifying child, 11% for two, 34% for three or more; no credit for filers without qualifying children
notes: TPC footnote 9: the Wisconsin credit is only available to workers with qualifying children. There is no single percentage, so percent is null. Wisconsin Department of Revenue FAQ: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-eic.aspx
